frase: I could've called you, but I didn't think you'd still be awake.
listen_for: Listen for the weak vowel in could've and the very short contraction you'd.
meaning_es: Podría haberte llamado, pero no pensé que todavía estarías despierto.

frase: You should've told me earlier instead of waiting until today.
listen_for: Should have is strongly reduced in natural speech and often sounds like one compact unit.
meaning_es: Deberías habérmelo dicho antes en vez de esperar hasta hoy.

frase: I would've gone with you if you'd asked me.
listen_for: Listen for the weak have in would've and the contraction you'd.
meaning_es: Habría ido contigo si me lo hubieras pedido.

frase: She might've left already, but I'm not completely sure.
listen_for: The word have is reduced and can be difficult to hear.
meaning_es: Puede que ya se haya ido, pero no estoy completamente seguro.

frase: There must've been a mistake somewhere in the system.
listen_for: The final consonants of must and the weak have can merge in fast speech.
meaning_es: Debe de haber habido algún error en el sistema.

frase: I don't know if I'll be able to finish it today.
listen_for: Listen for the linking between if and I'll, and the weak to.
meaning_es: No sé si podré terminarlo hoy.

frase: You won't be able to hear me if everyone keeps talking.
listen_for: Several words link across vowel and consonant boundaries.
meaning_es: No podrás oírme si todo el mundo sigue hablando.

frase: I'd rather stay here than drive for another two hours.
listen_for: I'd is very short; the important stress falls later in the phrase.
meaning_es: Preferiría quedarme aquí que conducir otras dos horas.

frase: We'd better leave now if we want to catch the last train.
listen_for: We'd better forms a common chunk, and the t in last may weaken before train.
meaning_es: Será mejor que salgamos ya si queremos coger el último tren.

frase: He doesn't usually eat breakfast, although he always has coffee.
listen_for: Listen to how the unstressed syllables become compressed.
meaning_es: Normalmente no desayuna, aunque siempre toma café.

frase: Can you pick it up on your way home?
listen_for: Pick it up flows as one unit through consonant-to-vowel linking.
meaning_es: ¿Puedes recogerlo de camino a casa?

frase: Could you turn it off before you leave?
listen_for: Could you may blend, and turn it off links across all three words.
meaning_es: ¿Podrías apagarlo antes de irte?

frase: I need to find out what happened before I make a decision.
listen_for: The final consonant of find links directly into out.
meaning_es: Necesito averiguar qué pasó antes de tomar una decisión.

frase: We ran out of milk, so I went to the shop.
listen_for: Ran out of is commonly heard as a continuous sequence rather than three separate words.
meaning_es: Nos quedamos sin leche, así que fui a la tienda.

frase: She came in and sat down without saying anything.
listen_for: Listen for linking in came in and the weak and between the two actions.
meaning_es: Entró y se sentó sin decir nada.

frase: I left it on the table next to your phone.
listen_for: Left it on contains several consecutive links and may sound very compressed.
meaning_es: Lo dejé en la mesa junto a tu teléfono.

frase: Take it away if you don't need it anymore.
listen_for: The three words connect smoothly with almost no pause between them.
meaning_es: Llévatelo si ya no lo necesitas.

frase: He looked at me and smiled without saying a word.
listen_for: Looked at links strongly, and and is usually very weak.
meaning_es: Me miró y sonrió sin decir una palabra.

frase: I saw an old friend when I was walking into town.
listen_for: Listen for linking across the word boundaries rather than separate words.
meaning_es: Vi a un viejo amigo cuando iba andando al centro.

frase: We need an answer before the end of the day.
listen_for: Need an links together, while of is normally unstressed.
meaning_es: Necesitamos una respuesta antes de que termine el día.

frase: What are you going to do when you get there?
listen_for: Going to may be strongly reduced in casual speech, and what are you is often compressed.
meaning_es: ¿Qué vas a hacer cuando llegues allí?

frase: Do you want to come with us after work?
listen_for: Want to is commonly reduced in casual speech, and do you may blend.
meaning_es: ¿Quieres venir con nosotros después del trabajo?

frase: I've got to leave in about ten minutes.
listen_for: Got to can be reduced, while in about links across the vowel.
meaning_es: Tengo que irme dentro de unos diez minutos.

frase: I have to get up early tomorrow morning.
listen_for: Have to often has a weak vowel, and get up links consonant to vowel.
meaning_es: Tengo que levantarme temprano mañana.

frase: It's kind of difficult to explain without showing you.
listen_for: Kind of is often compressed, and to becomes weak before explain.
meaning_es: Es un poco difícil de explicar sin enseñártelo.

frase: There are a lot of things we still need to discuss.
listen_for: Of and to are both weak forms here and may be hard to hear.
meaning_es: Todavía hay muchas cosas que tenemos que hablar.

frase: Let me know if you change your mind.
listen_for: Let me is often compressed into one smooth chunk.
meaning_es: Avísame si cambias de opinión.

frase: Give me a minute and I'll check it for you.
focus: give me; and I'll; for you
listen_for: Several grammatical words become weak, especially and and for.
meaning_es: Dame un minuto y te lo compruebo.

frase: Did you see what happened outside?
listen_for: Did you often blends strongly in natural speech.
meaning_es: ¿Viste lo que pasó fuera?

frase: Would you mind opening the window?
listen_for: Would you can blend into one compact sound sequence.
meaning_es: ¿Te importaría abrir la ventana?

frase: I missed the last train, so I had to get a taxi.
listen_for: The t in last may weaken before train, while had to is compressed.
meaning_es: Perdí el último tren, así que tuve que coger un taxi.

frase: We spent most of the day walking around the city.
listen_for: The t in most may weaken and of is unstressed.
meaning_es: Pasamos la mayor parte del día caminando por la ciudad.

frase: She asked me to send the report before lunch.
listen_for: The consonant cluster in asked me can simplify, while to is weak.
meaning_es: Me pidió que enviara el informe antes de comer.

frase: I don't know exactly what time we'll get back.
listen_for: Two adjacent t sounds in what time can merge into one.
meaning_es: No sé exactamente a qué hora volveremos.

frase: He used to work there when he was younger.
listen_for: Used to has a characteristic reduced pronunciation in connected speech.
meaning_es: Antes trabajaba allí cuando era más joven.

frase: I was just thinking about calling you.
listen_for: The final t in just may weaken before th, and about is unstressed.
meaning_es: Justo estaba pensando en llamarte.

frase: I can't believe you left the door open all night.
listen_for: The t in left can be weak before the, while all night links smoothly.
meaning_es: No puedo creer que dejaras la puerta abierta toda la noche.

frase: She told me she'd already finished the work.
listen_for: The contracted d links directly into the vowel at the start of already.
meaning_es: Me dijo que ya había terminado el trabajo.

frase: I asked you to wait outside for a minute.
focus: asked you; to wait; for a
listen_for: Asked you may blend strongly; to and for are weak forms.
meaning_es: Te pedí que esperaras fuera un minuto.

frase: We should probably leave before it gets too late.
listen_for: Should is unstressed and before it links consonant to vowel.
meaning_es: Probablemente deberíamos irnos antes de que sea demasiado tarde.

frase: I would've told you if I'd known you were coming.
listen_for: Two contractions plus weak function words make the sentence compact.
meaning_es: Te lo habría dicho si hubiera sabido que venías.

frase: You could've picked it up on your way home.
listen_for: A reduced modal-perfect form is followed by strong consonant-vowel linking.
meaning_es: Podrías haberlo recogido de camino a casa.

frase: I'm going to have to leave a little earlier tomorrow.
focus: going to; have to; a little
listen_for: Two common reductions appear close together in the same sentence.
meaning_es: Voy a tener que irme un poco antes mañana.

frase: What do you want to do about it?
focus: what do you; want to; about it
listen_for: Function words become weak and several boundaries disappear.
meaning_es: ¿Qué quieres hacer al respecto?

frase: You shouldn't have left it until the last minute.
focus: shouldn't have; left it; last minute
listen_for: Have is weak, left it links, and the t in last can weaken.
meaning_es: No deberías haberlo dejado hasta el último momento.

frase: There might've been something we could've done about it.
listen_for: Two modal-perfect contractions occur in the same sentence.
meaning_es: Puede que hubiera algo que podríamos haber hecho al respecto.

frase: Did you manage to pick it up before the shop closed?
focus: did you; to pick; pick it up
listen_for: Assimilation, a weak to, and consonant-vowel linking appear together.
meaning_es: ¿Conseguiste recogerlo antes de que cerrara la tienda?

frase: I'd have gone earlier if I'd known how busy it was.
focus: I'd have; if I'd; busy it
listen_for: The two contractions are very short and the surrounding words link.
meaning_es: Habría ido antes si hubiera sabido lo ocupado que estaba.

frase: We're going to run out of time if we don't leave soon.
focus: going to; run out of; time if
listen_for: A common reduction combines with a strongly linked phrasal verb.
meaning_es: Nos vamos a quedar sin tiempo si no salimos pronto.

frase: I don't know what you're talking about, but it sounds important.
focus: what you're; talking about; but it
listen_for: Listen for linking and weak unstressed syllables around the stressed words.
meaning_es: No sé de qué estás hablando, pero parece importante.
